name: deciding a change
from: A baselined thing changed by whoever was editing it: the baseline recording what the last person did rather than what the firm agreed, every downstream reader trusting a number nobody chose.
to: A change approved or refused by a cross-functional decision, priced at what it costs everyone rather than what it costs to make, its reason stated so a stranger can read it, and the approval sent to the configuration manager to be recorded — so a change in the baseline and a change through the board are the same set.
cost: The board's attention on every change however small, and the delay of routing a change through a decision instead of just making it — paid on purpose, because the alternative is paid by every reader forever.
otherwise: Changes reach the baseline around the record, the record cannot afterward tell which ones did, and the baseline degrades from what the firm agreed into what happened.
